accuracy.evidence: Graphemes and example words were checked against English Appendix 1, Year 1: ar (car, start, park, arm), or (for, short, born, horse), ore (more, score, before, shore), er (her, term, verb), ir (girl, bird, shirt, first) and ur (turn, hurt, church, burst). The adult text states correctly that in standard British English (non-rhotic) the r is not sounded separately, while in American English it is blended into the vowel, so cart has three phonemes either way. Every sound count in the items was checked by hand (star = s, t, ar; more = m, ore; car = c, ar).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips listed in the adult text: reading short vowel plus separate r (step 1 prediction 'Yes, the same'), letter reversals crat, gril, hrut (step 1 wrong slots, challenge 'order' and 'front'), confusing ir/ur/er (step 2 prediction 'No, they are different', step 4 girl/nurse, challenge gurl), mixing ar and or (step 2 boxes, fork/card), and counting letters not sounds (practice p2, mastery m4 and m8). Step 5 includes cat, where the r is wrong, so r is not added by habit.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagrvowel works on this topic's own mechanism: an r tile is slid into a gap between letter tiles and only the gap after the vowel turns the word into a real one (cat to cart, bun to burn, bid to bird, shot to short); the learner then taps the letters that make the single sound and chooses between same-sound spellings. The Vowel Digraphs, Trigraphs and phonics labs (flag_vowel.js, flag_trigraph.js, flag_phon.js) do not insert letters or treat ir/ur/er as one sound. lab_distinct passed under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the rule by doing: dropping r after the c returns 'crat is not a word. The r goes right after the vowel a, and then a and r make one sound: cart.' Sorting turn into the ar box returns 'turn has ur. ir, ur and er all make the same sound, like in her', so the one-sound idea is met in the sort before the summary. Done screens list cat + r = cart: a cart has wheels and the grapheme for each spotted word.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions each hold a tempting wrong answer: that the a in cart sounds like the a in cat (step 1 shows the new word), that bird and burn have different middle sounds (step 2 puts them in one box), and that girl and nurse are spelt the same way because they sound the same (step 4 shows ir and ur). The done line repeats the child's choice.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with nine distinct wrong-answer messages: no r so the vowel stays short (pack, bid, mop), or vs ar (pork), ar vs er (barn), ur for ir (gurl), r before the vowel (gril, hrut), r at the end (hutr), splitting the grapheme (fo, rk), and mere vs more. Each names the specific letters, e.g. 'ur makes the same sound, but girl is spelt with ir.'

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences with familiar words (Look at cat. Now put an r after the a. You get cart.) and read at FK grade 0.0 against the family limit of 5. Canvas words are 26 to 28 px on white tiles, one instruction line per round. The adult text names the graphemes, phonemes and the US term r-controlled syllable, at FK 8.9.

no_filler.evidence: The content gate found no banned phrases, and explanation overlap stayed under 12% against every lesson, including Vowel Digraphs, Trigraphs and Split Digraphs and Magic E. Each feedback line names the word and the letters; step texts are one instruction and one example.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android in light and iPhone 13 in dark for all six steps: the four or five letter tiles and their dashed r gaps fit on one row, the r tile sits below with room to drag, the three sound boxes fit side by side with up to four words each, and the ir/ur keys are 58 px tall; the button row wraps without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: The walkthrough gate completed all five tasks with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge showed, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in light or dark. Every drag or tap has a labelled button ('cat: put r after the a', 'farm: or (fork)', 'shirt: letter 3, i', 'Fill the gap with ir', 'Finish the sentence with cart'), and the canvas aria-label is rewritten with each feedback line. The r tile is #9a3412 on #ffedd5; words are dark ink on white.
